item.title: Error starting MCP Servers when running in .DevContainer or GitHub Codespaces

labels.name: info-needed
labels.description: Issue requires more information from poster

item.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.28.0
- VS Code Version: 1.101.0 & 1.102.0-insider
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 (Docker for Windows + is installed to host .devcontainers)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode with MCP
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): All models.
- Logs:
MCP server (filesystem, but all npx based MCPs fail to start):
2025-06-14 10:50:20.274 [info] Starting server filesystem
2025-06-14 10:50:20.276 [info] Connection state: Starting
2025-06-14 10:50:20.276 [info] Starting server from Remote extension host
2025-06-14 10:50:20.291 [info] Connection state: Starting
2025-06-14 10:50:20.292 [info] Connection state: Error spawn npx ENOENT

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create mcp.json in .vscode folder:
```json
{
    "servers": {
        "playwright": {
            "command": "npx",
            "args": [
                "-y",
                "@playwright/mcp@latest"
            ],
            "type": "stdio",
            "env": {}
        }
    }
}
```
2. Create .devcontainer/devcontainer.json
```json
{
    "name": "Azure Developer CLI",
    "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3",
    "features": {
        // See https://containers.dev/features for list of features
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/docker-in-docker:2": {},
        "ghcr.io/azure/azure-dev/azd:latest": {
            "version": "latest"
        },
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/azure-cli:1": {
            "version": "latest"
        },
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/python:1": {
            "version": "3.13",
            "installPip": true,
            "installPipx": true,
            "installPoetry": true,
            "installMyPy": true
        },
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/powershell:1": {
            "version": "latest",
            "installAzModule": true
        },
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node:1": {
            "version": "lts"
        },
        "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/dotnet:2": {
            "version": "8.0"
        }
    },
    "customizations": {
        "vscode": {
            "extensions": [
                "GitHub.vscode-github-actions",
                "ms-azuretools.azure-dev",
                "ms-azuretools.vscode-bicep",
                "ms-azuretools.vscode-docker",
                "TeamsDevApp.vscode-ai-foundry",
                "ms-python.vscode-pylance",
                "ms-python.pylint",
                "ms-python.python",
                "ms-toolsai.jupyter",
                "dbaeumer.vscode-eslint",
                "ms-python.black-formatter",
                "ms-playwright.playwright",
                "ms-dotnettools.csharp",
                "ms-dotnettools.csdevkit"
            ]
        }
    },
    "forwardPorts": [
        // Forward ports if needed for local development
    ],
    "postCreateCommand": "./.devcontainer/post-create.sh",
    "remoteUser": "vscode",
    "hostRequirements": {
        "memory": "8gb"
    }
}
```
3. Create post-create.sh (using to verify that NPM/NPX etc is in .devcontainer):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Post-create command script for Azure AI Foundry Jumpstart dev container
# This script is executed after the dev container is created

set -e  # Exit on any error

echo "🚀 Running post-create setup for Azure AI Foundry Jumpstart devcontainer..."

# Configure Git settings
echo "📝 Configuring Git settings..."
git config --global core.autocrlf input
git config --global core.fileMode false

# Install Python development dependencies
echo "🐍 Installing Python development dependencies..."
pip3 install -r ./requirements-dev.txt

# Ensure Node.js tools are properly sourced and available
echo "🔧 Setting up Node.js environment..."
# Source nvm to ensure it's available
if [ -s "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh" ]; then
    . "${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh"
    echo "  NVM sourced successfully"
else
    echo "  Warning: NVM not found at ${NVM_DIR}/nvm.sh"
fi

# Verify installations
echo "✅ Verifying installations..."
echo "  Node.js version: $(node --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'Not found')"
echo "  NPM version: $(npm --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'Not found')"
echo "  NPX version: $(npx --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'Not found')"
echo "  NPX location: $(which npx 2>/dev/null || echo 'Not found')"
echo "  Python version: $(python3 --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'Not found')"

echo "🎉 Post-create setup completed successfully!"
```

4. Open repo in VS Code.
5. CTRL+SHIFT+P in VS Code and select: DevContainer: Reopen in Container (can also repro this in GitHub Code Spaces)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0ed37a7-0180-42df-9f7d-963a7823fbe9)
6. Once repo opened in container, open mcp.json and try to start any of the MCP servers:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28054e2f-2e41-4f12-ba7e-48822fb92136)

7. Have confirmed that npx is in the .devcontainer and in the path. Putting full path to npx doesn't resolve either.

There aren't any commands that can be found when running MCP in .devcontainer/GitHub Codespaces. Here is the example repo I'm using: https://github.com/PlagueHO/azure-ai-foundry-jumpstart/blob/main/.vscode/mcp.json

Would love a fix or work around.
